note: Entry point of the feature-research -> feature-plan -> feature-implement pipeline. Running these against feature-research also exercises the chain, since the skill hands off to feature-plan (and feature-plan to feature-implement) once each gate is satisfied.

evals.prompt: I want to add a feature that lets event-type owners set a custom "thank you" message that shows on the booking confirmation page after someone books. Can you build this?
evals.expected_output: Claude interviews for the spec and searches the codebase for comparable existing patterns, writes docs/plans/<slug>/research.md following the template, then hands off to feature-plan which writes docs/plans/<slug>/plan.md and stops for approval before any code is touched. It does not jump straight into editing source files.

evals.prompt: We need to let team admins bulk-export their team's bookings as a CSV from the bookings page. Walk me through developing this.
evals.expected_output: Claude asks scoping questions (columns, date range, permissions, large-dataset handling), records codebase findings in research.md, hands off to feature-plan for a plan.md with real implementation steps naming files/procedures, and that skill stops for approval. If approved, feature-implement adds Vitest tests, runs scoped type-check/lint/build/tests and reports results, then drafts docs/plans/<slug>/pr.md from .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md.

evals.prompt: Add a user setting so people can choose whether cancelled bookings still show up in their calendar view or get hidden. Develop the whole thing.
evals.expected_output: Claude interviews for the spec (default value, per-user vs per-calendar, migration of existing users), writes research.md, hands off to feature-plan which addresses the data-model/migration question and waits for approval. The final PR description (from feature-implement) follows the repo template including the Mandatory Tasks checkboxes and a filled-in "How should this be tested?" section.
